2. Heard Sri Jitendra Narayan Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
3.
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 205 of 2024, under Section 376(2)(i) of I.P.C., Police Station - Bewar, District - Mainpuri, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have committed rape with the deaf, dumb and blind sister of the informant in the night of 10/11.06.2024 at about 01:00 AM.
The informant has called his neighbour Rajkishor and both of them saw the applicant without clothes.

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the FIR is delayed by about 12 hours and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

The conduct of the informant seems to be unnatural as he instead of resisting the offence of rape being with his sister, has called his neighbour Rajkishor to the place of occurrence and seeing both of them, the applicant is stated to have run away from the place of occurrence.
6. Learned counsel has further argued that the victim is major aged about 22 years.
There is no medical corroboration of the incident.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present as he did not want to repay the loan taken from the informant.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 12.06.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. Per contra, learned State Law Officer has vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim is a deaf, dumb and blind girl and she did not know the consequences.
She could not raise any alarm as she is dumb and the applicant has taken advantage of her precarious conditions.
Even the Indian Penal Code provides that the consent of such kind of a person shall not be deemed to be the consent in the eyes of law, as such, the applicant is not entitled for bail.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and the fact that the victim is a deaf, dumb and blind lady coupled by the fact that the FIR is prompt, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
9. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

10. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, in view of the principle laid down in the recent judgements of the Supreme Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar vs. State of Punjab 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
